hand-pinky-up.context: A closed fist with only the little finger raised straight up. Used for pinky promises, fancy tea drinking jokes, small or tiny sizes and playful gesture reactions.

c-shape-hand.context: A hand seen from the side with the thumb and fingers curved into an open letter C. Used for sign language, the letter C, cup or grip shapes and measuring the width of an object.

hands-forming-roof.context: Two flat hands meeting at the fingertips in a peaked roof over a small person. Used for shelter, housing support, home insurance, safety nets and care services.

hand-binoculars.context: Two hands curled into tubes and held side by side in front of the eyes like binoculars. Used for searching, looking far away, lookout, spying and exploring.

talking-hand-gesture.context: A hand shaped like a talking mouth with the fingers above and the thumb below, and short speech lines at the opening. Used for chatter, blah blah, gossip, someone who talks too much and endless talk.

palm-note.context: An open palm facing the viewer with short scribbled lines written across it. Used for notes on the hand, quick reminders, cheat sheets and things to remember.

wrap-it-up-gesture.context: A raised index finger drawing a circle in the air, shown by a circular arrow around the fingertip. Used for wrap it up, hurry up, time to finish, round up and start over.

hand-span.context: An open hand with the fingers spread wide beneath a double-headed arrow running from the thumb to the little finger. Used for hand span, measuring by hand, reach, stretch and size by hand.

triple-tap-gesture.context: A pointing finger with a tap ripple beside the number 3. Used for triple tap touch controls, three taps to zoom, accessibility shortcuts and gesture guides on touchscreens.

two-finger-tap-gesture.context: A hand with two fingers raised together and tap ripples above the fingertips. Used for two finger tap and right click on trackpads and touchscreens, and for gesture guides.

three-finger-swipe-gesture.context: A hand with three fingers raised under a long arrow pointing to the side. Used for three finger swipes on trackpads and touchscreens, switching apps or pages and gesture guides.

flick-gesture.context: A fingertip with a quick curved flick stroke leaving it and speed lines trailing the stroke. Used for flick, fling and fast scroll gestures and for throwing items across a screen.

edge-swipe-gesture.context: A phone outline with a fingertip at its side edge and a short arrow pointing inward from the bezel. Used for edge swipe and back gestures, side panels and gesture navigation guides.

drag-and-drop-gesture.context: A fingertip holding a small tile that follows a short path toward a dashed drop target square. Used for drag and drop, moving items, reordering and upload drop zones.

force-press-gesture.context: A fingertip pressing hard on a surface inside layered pressure rings, with a small downward arrow above. Used for force press, deep press and pressure sensitive touch menus.

draw-gesture.context: A fingertip at the end of a looping freehand line that starts from a small dot. Used for drawing with a finger, sketching, doodling, signing on a screen and handwriting input.

pattern-unlock.context: A three by three grid of dots with a connected line drawn through several of them. Used for pattern lock screens, swipe to unlock and simple phone security settings.

tilt-phone-gesture.context: A phone tilted at an angle with a curved double-headed arrow beside its top corner. Used for tilt controls, motion sensing, gyroscope features and shake or rotate device prompts.

raise-to-wake.context: A wrist wearing a smartwatch lifted along a curved arrow with the watch face lit up. Used for raise to wake, wrist raise settings, always on display and wearable gesture guides.

multi-touch-gesture.context: Five fingertip touch points spread in the arc of a hand on a rounded trackpad surface. Used for multi-touch, five finger gestures and touch surface settings.

back-tap-gesture.context: The back of a phone with a camera bump and a finger tapping the back panel. Used for back tap shortcuts, double tap on the rear of a phone and accessibility settings.

hand-on-mouse.context: A hand seen from above resting on a computer mouse with the index finger on the left button. Used for desk work, clicking, computer use, mouse settings and workstation ergonomics.

data-glove.context: A glove with sensor dots across the knuckles and a short cable leading from the cuff. Used for virtual reality gloves, haptic feedback, motion capture and hand tracking hardware.

palm-push.context: A flat palm pressing against the side of a square block, with short motion lines beyond the block. Used for pushing, effort, shoving, moving heavy things and force.

tearing-paper.context: A sheet of paper pulled apart into two halves along a jagged tear. Used for tearing up documents, cancelling, torn or broken agreements, break ups and rip actions.

crumpling-paper.context: A hand squeezing a crumpled ball of paper, with angular creases showing above the fingers. Used for discarded drafts, rejected ideas, waste paper and starting over.

peeling-sticker.context: A finger lifting the curled corner of a square sticker off a surface. Used for peeling labels and decals, removing stickers, peel off backing and adhesive products.

stress-ball-squeeze.context: A hand clenched around a round ball that bulges out above and beside the fingers. Used for stress relief, squeezing a stress ball, grip exercise and anxiety tools.

house-in-hand.context: An open palm held up with a small house resting on it. Used for home ownership, mortgages, housing support, real estate services and looking after a home.

idea-in-hand.context: An open palm held up with a lightbulb standing on it and short rays around the bulb. Used for ideas, innovation, inspiration, tips and offering a solution.

checking-for-rain.context: An open palm held out face up with a few raindrops falling onto it from above. Used for checking the weather, rain forecasts, drizzle and is it raining prompts.

carrying-briefcase.context: A hand gripping the top handle of a briefcase that hangs below it. Used for commuting, business travel, going to work, professional services and office jobs.

hand-holding-flashlight.context: A hand gripping a flashlight with a widening beam of light from its head. Used for searching in the dark, inspections, power cuts, camping and night time safety.

pointing-remote.context: A hand holding a remote control pointed forward with two signal arcs coming from its tip. Used for television controls, infrared remotes, smart home control and switching channels.

reading-with-finger.context: An index finger resting under one line of text on a page that has more lines above and below. Used for following text, early reading, literacy help and proofreading.

turning-page.context: A hand lifting the corner of the right page of an open book as it curls over. Used for turning a page, reading progress, next page controls and e-book page flips.

baby-grasping-finger.context: A tiny baby hand wrapped around the tip of a larger adult index finger. Used for newborns, parenting, family bonds, baby care and the grasp reflex.

comforting-hand.context: One hand resting gently on top of another hand with a small heart above them. Used for comfort, sympathy, emotional support, reassurance and caring gestures.

launching-paper-plane.context: A hand releasing a paper plane forward with a dotted flight trail behind it. Used for throwing a paper plane, launching ideas, sending off messages and play.

cutting-with-scissors.context: Open scissors cutting along a dashed line into a sheet of paper. Used for cutting, crafts, coupons, cut here lines, trimming and paper projects.

erasing-pencil-mark.context: A hand rubbing an eraser over a smudged pencil line with small crumbs scattered beside it. Used for erasing mistakes, corrections, drawing and editing and undoing written work.

shielding-flame.context: A cupped hand curved around one side of a candle flame to block the wind. Used for protecting something fragile, keeping hope alive, vigils and care in hard conditions.

breaking-chains.context: A chain snapped at its middle link with the two halves pulled apart and small spark lines above the break. Used for freedom, breaking free, liberation, escape and ending restrictions.

flicking-lighter.context: A hand holding a pocket lighter with the thumb on the wheel and a small flame on top. Used for lighting a flame, smokers, candles, campfires and fire related services.

threading-needle.context: A thumb and finger holding the end of a thread pointed at the eye of an upright sewing needle. Used for sewing, tailoring, mending clothes and crafts.

petting-dog.context: A hand resting flat on top of a dog's head with two small curved stroke marks above it. Used for petting pets, dog care, animal shelters, therapy animals and affection.
